parsed.process: manual cork-oak bark stripping with a hand axe (machado)
parsed.current_inefficiency: success depends entirely on the harvester's skill; cutting too deep severs the cambium and harms the tree, while larger intact sheets are worth more, so depth and split-avoidance must be judged by feel in real time
parsed.ai_technique: real-time acoustic/vibration sensing on the axe handle classified by a lightweight 1D-CNN (acoustic-emission classification), analogous to tool-wear and material-boundary detection used in CNC machining
parsed.how_it_improves: a contact accelerometer/piezo mic on the machado streams vibration as the edge is twisted between cork and cambium -> a 1D-CNN trained on labeled strokes (good pry vs. cambium-contact vs. cork-tearing) infers in <50 ms which layer the edge is engaging -> a haptic buzz or LED on the handle warns the moment the signal shifts toward cambium-cutting or sheet-splitting -> harvester eases off before damaging the tree or fracturing the sheet, raising intact-sheet yield and reducing tree injury without replacing the human
parsed.why_not_done_before: acoustic-emission boundary sensing is mature in metal/wood CNC but nobody has collected the niche labeled dataset of cork-vs-cambium stroke signatures; the harvest is seasonal, decentralized among traditional artisans, low-margin, and outsiders assumed the only AI play was full robotic stripping (which failed), so the narrow handle-sensor assist was overlooked
parsed.primary_quote: success depends entirely on the harvester's skill

reasoning_trace.reasoning: The core skill is a tactile/auditory judgment of when the edge has reached the cambium boundary and when the sheet is about to split — exactly the signal that acoustic-emission/vibration sensing captures in CNC tool-material monitoring. A handle-mounted accelerometer is cheap, robust to the bark dust and outdoor conditions that would foul a vision system buried under the lifting sheet, and gives the millisecond-latency feedback a swinging axe needs. I rejected hyperspectral/CV cork-cambium imaging because during the pry the boundary is occluded by the lifting cork and the worker's hands, so a camera can't see the cut plane; vibration travels straight up the tool from the cut. The narrow assist (warn the human) respects R13 rather than automating stripping.
reasoning_trace.decision: instrument the machado with a vibration sensor + 1D-CNN that classifies the cutting layer in real time and gives haptic warning before cambium damage or sheet splitting
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - the sensing modality is proven in CNC, but feasibility hinges on whether cork-vs-cambium strokes produce separable vibration signatures, which is unverified for this material
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: cork's softness damps the edge-engagement vibrations below the noise of the swing/twist so the signatures aren't separable, or expert harvesters are already accurate enough that the marginal yield gain doesn't justify instrumenting the tool
